item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 021716
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Wed Sep 2 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands, and on Tropical Storm Marie, located several
hundred miles south-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of southwestern
Mexico over the weekend. Gradual development is possible during the
early to middle part of next week as the system moves
west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, and is likely to remain well
offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.8N 132.8W
ABOUT 1455 MI...2340 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...145 MPH...230 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...940 MB...27.76 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Karina was located
near latitude 18.8 North, longitude 132.8 West. Karina is moving
toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h) and a westward to
west-northwestward motion is expected over the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 145 mph (230 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Karina is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Some fluctuations in intensity are possible 
today, followed by slow weakening over the next several days. 
However, Karina is likely to remain a powerful hurricane the next 
couple of days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 940 mb (27.76 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 25
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Wed Sep 02 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 021435
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  25
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 AM HST Wed Sep 02 2026
 
Karina continues to exhibit a circular, annular structure on 
proxy-vis and infrared satellite imagery. The hurricane has a 
well-defined, warm 30 n mi eye, with deep convection wrapping around 
the inner core. The latest objective and subjective satellite 
intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS and TAFB range from 109 to 137 kt. 
Based on the steady satellite appearance and a range of these 
estimates, the intensity is held at 125 kt.
 
The hurricane continues to move westward at an estimated motion of 
285/9 kt. The steering flow remains unchanged, with the system 
expected to continue moving westward to west-northwestward along the 
southern side of a ridge located to the north. As a mid-level low 
moves north of the Hawaiian islands the ridge will weaken, and the 
system should move northwestward. The latest NHC track is similar 
to the previous and lies close to the HCCA and GDMI aids.
 
Karina remains over marginally warm waters sea surface temperatures, 
tracking roughly parallel to the 26-27C isotherm. Wind shear also 
remains low during the next few days, before increasing beyond 72 h. 
Some fluctuations in intensity are possible today, before a gradual 
weakening trend is expected. In about 2-3 days, the system should 
begin to move into a drier environment and over cooler SSTs, 
although given the annular structure, weakening is anticipated to be 
more gradual than normal. The NHC intensity guidance is higher than 
most of the guidance, given the annular structure, and shows a 
gradual rate of weakening during the early part of the forecast 
period before a more steady rate of weakening by the end of the 
period. Global infrared simulated satellite imagery shows that 
Karina will struggle to produce organized deep convection by day 5, 
due to the shear and dry air, and the NHC forecast now calls for the 
system to become post-tropical at that time.

NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026

...MARIE A LITTLE STRONGER...
...EXPECTED TO BECOME A HURRICANE LATER TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.1N 111.7W
ABOUT 415 MI...670 KM SSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...992 MB...29.30 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Marie was
located near latitude 17.1 North, longitude 111.7 West. Marie is
moving toward the northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A turn toward the
west-northwest is expected by tonight, and that motion should
continue through the weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 70 mph (110 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Some strengthening is forecast through Friday, 
and Marie is likely to become a hurricane later today.  A gradual 
weakening trend is expected over the weekend.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles (295 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 992 mb (29.30 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will affect portions of the coast of 
southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next few 
days and will likely spread northward to southern California over 
the weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf 
and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local 
weather office. A depiction of rip current risk for the United 
States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Roberts

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Forecast Discussion Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Wed Sep 02 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 021436
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Marie Discussion Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 AM MST Wed Sep 02 2026
 
Conventional satellite animation and microwave images indicate that 
Marie's cloud pattern has improved during the past several hours.  
An impressive primary spiral band with cold cloud tops of -83C 
resides on the eastern half of the cyclone, and inner core deep 
convection continues to become better organized.  A compromise of 
TAFB's Dvorak satellite intensity estimate and the CIMSS objective 
estimates yields an initial intensity of 60 kt for this advisory.
 
Favorable environmental conditions along with warm sea surface 
temperatures should allow for further strengthening during the 
couple of days.  By the weekend, the Decay-SHIPS 
statistical/dynamical intensity guidance and the global models 
indicate that Marie will encounter a drier, stable marine layer air 
mass while moving over progressively cooler oceanic temperatures.  
The NHC intensity forecast is close to the HFIP HCCA consensus and 
just above the IVCN consensus aid.

Marie's initial motion is estimated to be northwest, or 305/8 kt, 
and this general motion should continue through today.  Afterward, 
subtropical high pressure over northern Mexico/Baja California 
peninsula is expected to build westward over the extreme eastern 
Pacific, steering the cyclone generally west-northwestward.  Over 
the weekend, the above-mentioned ridge should weaken some, and model 
guidance cross-track uncertainty remains due to two possible 
synoptic pattern solutions.  A few of the regional models 
(HWRF/HMON/TC-COAMPS) and the UKMET indicate an amplifying mid- to 
upper-level trough capturing Marie and steering the cyclone toward 
the northwest to north.  The majority of the guidance, on the other 
hand, show a cut-off upper low developing well to the north over the 
eastern Pacific but allowing enough ridging to maintain north of the 
cyclone.  The official track forecast favors the latter solution and 
lies between the HCCA consensus and the Google DeepMind FNv3 
ensemble mean.
